- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent 7-day mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 10-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.1) after a downtrend, model may lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch upward momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 10% above 30d true mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30d horizon, model often overweights recent volatility; use 14-day EWMA instead of 30d average for smoothing.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to compensate.
